digest.top_line: TNTCRT: 3yr DFS 74.8% v 66.0%, HR 0.674 (0.489-0.929) for doublet-LC TNT, but locoregional failure identical (6.03% v 6.19%).
digest.tldr: Rectal owned the day, and both trials say the same thing to a rad onc: the RT question is settled, the sequencing question isn't. TNTCRT moved DFS entirely through distant control with LRR flat; STELLAR showed 5x5Gy IMRT non-inferior to 50Gy/25fx (3y LRR 8.4% v 11.0%) with toxicity driven by chemo, not RT. Prostate stayed imaging-only: PSMA PET still not a validated response biomarker.

sites.intro: Both items are PSMA PET interpretation, not therapy: androgen-axis regulation of PSMA expression and BCR natural history off treatment.

studies.name: USPCC 2026 Point-Counterpoint: PSMA PET as Response Assessment
studies.tldr: Conference point-counterpoint arguing PSMA uptake tracks AR signaling, not tumor burden, so serial PSMA PET is not yet a response biomarker.
details: 🔍 USPCC 2026 point-counterpoint session (Steven Rowe, UT Southwestern); position: PSMA PET has no present role in response assessment
🔍 Core argument: PSMA expression is dynamically regulated by the androgen axis, not a static marker of tumor burden
📊 Zukotynski 18F-DCFPyL trial (n=16 evaluable, pre-ARSI and 2-4 mo post): median time to therapy change 9.6 mo (95% CI 6.9-14.2)
📊 Same cohort: median OS 28.6 mo (95% CI 18.3-NA)

details.text: 📊 Uptake-change metrics stratify outcomes (Zukotynski, 18F-DCFPyL pre/post ARSI)

details: ⚠️ Both HR CIs are enormous (1.17-21.65 and 1.81-47.87) off 16 pts; prognostic separation, not a validated response metric
📊 Markowski BAT series: 6 men imaged at baseline and 3 mo, 3 progressed; PSMA PET flagged progression earlier than conventional imaging
⚠️ Flare vs true progression is unresolved: ADT/ARSI initiation itself moves PSMA expression, so an early rising SUV is uninterpretable as burden

🔍 Repeatability data reviewed (Bland-Altman, ICC, within-subject CV) across SUVmax, SUVmean, SUVtotal, tumor volume; lesion identification and segmentation variability flagged as limiting serial quantitation
🔗 RECIP 1.0 (Gafita, JNM 2022) offered as the counterweight: PET plus CT categories (PD/PR/SD/CR) built for post-radioligand response, still needing validation outside that setting
❓ Take-home: kinetics of androgen-axis effects on PSMA and AI-assisted lesion detection are the named prerequisites
studies.significance: For an RT reader the operative caution is oligomet SBRT selection: if a post-ADT scan drives whether to treat 3 lesions or 5, ARSI-induced uptake change can move lesion count without moving disease. RECIP 1.0 was built for post-radioligand response, not for pre-SBRT target selection.
studies.monday_clinic: For a man on an ARSI or BAT whose restaging PSMA PET is being read as response or progression, this argues the scan's uptake change is confounded by androgen-axis effects on PSMA expression; it does not question PSMA PET for initial staging or lesion detection in an untreated or hormone-naive setting.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Bears on metastasis-directed therapy: a restaging PSMA PET after ARSI start can change apparent lesion count and SUV without a change in burden, which is exactly the input to oligomet SBRT target selection. RECIP 1.0 was validated post-radioligand, not for pre-SBRT planning.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Argues against treating a rising or falling SUV as an ARSI response signal. Uptake-change metrics were prognostic (DPSM HR 5.03, DASM HR 9.31) in 16 pts, but prognostic separation is not a response endpoint, and the CIs are wide enough that no line-of-therapy switch should hang on them.

open_questions: Kinetics of androgen-axis therapy effects on PSMA expression
RECIP validation outside the radioligand-therapy setting
Reproducibility of AI-assisted lesion identification and segmentation

studies.name: PSMA-PET BCR Natural History Study
studies.tldr: Baseline of first 130 PSMA-positive BCR men: most with PSA-DT >9-12mo still show PET lesions, yet ~2/3 observed off therapy.
details: 🔍 Prospective NCI natural-history cohort; baseline data on first 130 pts, study ongoing, median f/u ~2 yrs
🔍 Eligibility: BCR after definitive therapy, all post-salvage RT or declined it; PSA ≥0.5 required for entry
🔍 Imaging schedule: baseline PSMA PET; negative → annual, any finding (incl. equivocal) → q6mo
📊 Only ~1/3 of pts have gone on therapy; the majority are observed off treatment
📊 Vast majority of pts with PSA-DT >9mo and >12mo had PSMA PET findings when PSA >5
📊 Sites described: nodal disease, prostate-bed recurrence, occasional small equivocal bone lesions
📊 Companion Madan poster: conventional-imaging progression in 5 of the first ~150 pts at ~1.5yr f/u
📊 >95% had no abrupt PET change discordant with PSA/PSA-DT behavior
⚠️ Baseline cross-sectional read only; no per-arm outcomes, no HR, no effect size reported in source
⚠️ Therapy not mandated: intermittent ADT, ARPI, SBRT, Radium-223 trials all permitted, so any evolution signal is confounded
⚠️ Single-center NCI referral cohort; enrichment for trial-seeking pts limits generalizability
⚠️ Source is a conference video interview, not a peer-reviewed report; numbers are spoken approximations

verdict.rationale: Single-arm observational cohort, baseline cross-section of 130 pts, no outcome endpoint reached; heterogeneous permitted therapies. Descriptive only, cannot define who safely defers treatment.
verdict.audience: PSMA-positive biochemically recurrent prostate ca, post-definitive + salvage…

studies.significance: The RT-relevant read is that these men are all post-salvage-RT failures, so PET-detected nodal and prostate-bed lesions land squarely in the metastasis-directed-therapy decision. SBRT was permitted, not protocolized, and no per-lesion local control is reported in source, so this bounds the observation arm rather than defining an SBRT indication.
studies.monday_clinic: In PSMA-positive BCR after definitive therapy and salvage RT with slow PSA doubling time, this supports observation as a defensible option rather than reflex systemic therapy for PET-only findings; it does not speak to men with rapid doubling times or conventional-imaging metastases.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Prospective **natural history** cohort at the NCI following men with PSMA-positive BCR with serial PSMA PET. Data presented are the **baseline cross-section of the first 130 pts**; median follow-up is about **2 years** with interim longitudinal data still pending.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Recurrence after definitive therapy, with **salvage radiation already delivered or declined** in post-prostatectomy pts. Entry requires **PSA ≥0.5**. Explicitly framed as a state that would not have qualified for historical metastatic trials, since the disease is invisible on conventional imaging.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: Salvage RT is a prior-therapy gate rather than a study intervention. On study, **SBRT is permitted** alongside any therapy lasting under six months; dose, fractionation and target volume are **not reported in source**.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: This analysis relates **baseline PSMA PET findings to PSA doubling time**, the field's working risk metric in BCR. Longitudinal endpoints (PET evolution, conventional-imaging progression) are the stated goal but not yet reported.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Most pts with **PSA-DT >9mo and >12mo** still had PSMA PET findings once **PSA exceeded 5**, chiefly nodal, prostate-bed, and small equivocal bone lesions. **About one third** started therapy; the rest were observed. A companion analysis found conventional-imaging progression in **5 of ~150 pts** at roughly 1.5yr, and **>95%** showed no PET change discordant with PSA kinetics.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents PSMA-positive BCR after definitive therapy including salvage RT, PSA ≥0.5, largely slow PSA doubling time. Does not represent conventional-imaging mCSPC, de novo metastatic disease, or PSMA-negative BCR.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Therapy was physician-choice and time-limited rather than randomized, so PET evolution mixes treated and untreated pts. All numbers here come from a **spoken conference interview**, not a peer-reviewed dataset, and the 130-pt baseline slice cannot yet separate indolent from lethal PSMA-positive BCR.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The framing argument is that PSMA PET created a **disease state, not new disease**: these men existed in historical BCR trials, undetected. The overtreatment risk the investigators name is real, since mCSPC doublet or triplet approaches are being applied to pts whose natural history may run many years untreated.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Every pt here has already failed or declined salvage RT, so PET-positive nodes and bed recurrences are the exact population being offered metastatic-directed SBRT. SBRT was allowed but not protocolized and no local control data is reported in source, so this cohort argues for a defensible observation comparator rather than an SBRT indication.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: The signal is against reflex mCSPC-style systemic therapy for PET-only disease: about a third went on therapy, and conventional-imaging progression hit 5 of ~150 pts at 1.5yr. Intermittent ADT and ARPI approaches were used selectively, framing PSA doubling time, not PET positivity alone, as the trigger.

open_questions: Which PSMA PET features predict conventional-imaging progression
Whether observation is safe in PSMA-positive BCR with fast doubling time
Role of metastasis-directed SBRT vs observation in PET-only recurrence

sites.intro: Two phase III LARC trials, both keeping RT constant within arm: TNTCRT tests the chemo backbone under LCRT, STELLAR tests 5x5Gy against 50Gy/25fx, and neither moves locoregional failure.

studies.name: TNTCRT
studies.tldr: 3yr DFS 74.8% v 66.0%, HR 0.674 (0.489-0.929), P=.016 for doublet-LC TNT over nCRT in high-risk LARC.
details: 🔍 Phase 3 multicenter RCT, N=458 (232 doublet-LC TNT v 226 nCRT), enrolled Jun 2017 to Dec 2023, median f/u 51mo
🔍 Eligibility: stage II/III LARC, age 18-70, ≥1 MRI high-risk feature (cT4a-b, cN2, MRF+, or cT3c-d with EMVI)
🔍 High-risk enrichment real: cT4 47.82%, cN2 75.98%, threatened MRF 70.96%, EMVI 54.80%
💊 Experimental: 1 cycle induction CAPOX → LCRT with 2 cycles concurrent CAPOX → 3 cycles consolidation CAPOX → TME
💊 Control: LCRT with concurrent capecitabine → TME → 6 cycles adjuvant CAPOX starting 4-8wk post-op
⚠️ RT dose/fractionation and target volume not reported in source text; both arms got LCRT, so the trial isolates the chemo backbone, not the RT question

details.text: 📊 Efficacy and safety, doublet-LC TNT v nCRT

details: 📊 TME rate ~87% doublet-LC TNT v ~90% nCRT after neoadjuvant therapy
🔗 Sits alongside RAPIDO, PRODIGE-23, STELLAR; unlike RAPIDO/STELLAR this keeps LCRT rather than short-course, so the LCRT-v-SCRT question stays open
⚠️ All benefit is distant: MFS moved, locoregional failure did not (6.03% v 6.19%), and OS is not separated at 51mo
⚠️ Age cap 70; benefit-risk in older pts untested per the authors

verdict.rationale: Randomised phase 3, primary DFS endpoint met with adequate follow-up, but supports an already-recognized TNT paradigm rather than displacing it; OS immature.
verdict.audience: Stage II/III rectal, ≥1 MRI high-risk feature (cT4, cN2, MRF+, EMVI), age ≤70

studies.significance: Locoregional failure was identical (6.03% v 6.19%, P=.943) while MFS moved (77.7% v 67.6%), so intensifying the concurrent and sandwich chemo buys distant control, not local control, on an unchanged LCRT backbone. RT dose and target volume are not in the source text, which limits transfer. The decision this moves is chemo intensity around RT, not the RT prescription.
studies.monday_clinic: In stage II/III rectal cancer aged 70 or younger with an MRI high-risk feature (cT4, cN2, threatened MRF, or EMVI), this supports doublet CAPOX delivered around long-course RT rather than concurrent capecitabine plus adjuvant chemo; it does not speak to low-risk cT3 disease, pts over 70, or short-course TNT.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Multicenter randomized **phase 3**, N=**458** (doublet-LC TNT n=232, nCRT n=226), accrual June 2017 to December 2023, median follow-up **51 months**. **Primary:** disease-free survival.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Stage II/III LARC aged **18 to 70** with at least **1 MRI high-risk feature**: cT4a-b, cN2, mesorectal fascia involvement, or cT3c-d with extramural vascular invasion. Baseline burden was genuinely high risk: cT4 **47.82%**, cN2 **75.98%**, threatened MRF **70.96%**, EMVI **54.80%**.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: Experimental arm: 1 cycle induction **CAPOX**, then LCRT with 2 cycles concurrent CAPOX, then 3 cycles consolidation CAPOX, then surgery. Control arm: LCRT with **concurrent capecitabine**, surgery, then 6 cycles adjuvant CAPOX beginning 4 to 8 weeks postoperatively.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **Long-course RT in both arms**; the randomisation changes the chemotherapy around it, not the radiation. Dose, fractionation, and target volume are **not reported in source text**.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary:** DFS. **Secondary** reported here: MFS, pCR, locoregional failure, overall survival, grade ≥3 adverse events, major postoperative complications.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Primary endpoint met; the distant-versus-local split is the read, with **locoregional failure unchanged** and OS not yet separated (P=.167). See the arm-by-arm table above.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: Neoadjuvant grade ≥3 AEs roughly tripled (**27.59% v 8.56%**, P<.001), but across the entire treatment course the difference washed out (28.02% v 24.32%, P=.371) because the control arm's toxicity was deferred to adjuvant CAPOX. Major postoperative complications were comparable (3.98% v 2.94%).

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents high-risk stage II/III LARC aged 70 or younger with MRI-defined cT4, cN2, threatened MRF, or EMVI. Does not represent pts over 70, low-risk cT3N0-1 disease, or short-course RT-based TNT schedules.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: The authors position this against **RAPIDO**, **PRODIGE-23**, and **STELLAR**, and explicitly call for comparison against short-course RT-based or nondoublet-concurrent TNT regimens. The phase 2 predecessor of this regimen reported a **36.2%** complete response rate.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: The control arm's adjuvant chemo is a **known weak link** (delivery after TME is unreliable), so part of the DFS gap may reflect chemo received rather than sequencing itself. Single-country accrual over 6.5 years, no reported organ-preservation or functional endpoints yet, and **OS remains immature** at 51 months.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: The RT prescription is the constant, not the variable: LCRT in both arms, and locoregional failure was identical (6.03% v 6.19%, P=.943) despite a pCR jump to 26.37%. So the higher pCR does not translate into local control here, and with dose, fractionation, and target volume absent from source text, this does not move the RT prescription. It does keep LCRT viable in the TNT era where RAPIDO and STELLAR pushed short course.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: The real randomisation is chemo delivery: sandwiched CAPOX around RT versus concurrent capecitabine plus 6 cycles of postoperative CAPOX. Sandwiching moved MFS (77.7% v 67.6%, HR 0.655) at the cost of tripled neoadjuvant grade ≥3 toxicity (27.59% v 8.56%), though whole-course severe toxicity was comparable (28.02% v 24.32%). This informs when to give the oxaliplatin, not whether.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: Intensified neoadjuvant therapy did not degrade the operation: major postoperative complications 3.98% v 2.94% (P=.567). Roughly 87% versus 90% went on to TME, and pCR rose to 26.37% from 9.80%, which is the rate that feeds watch-and-wait discussions, though no organ-preservation endpoint is reported in source.

open_questions: Doublet-LC TNT versus short-course RT-based TNT
Whether higher pCR translates to organ preservation

studies.name: STELLAR
studies.tldr: 3y DFS 64.5% vs 62.3%, HR 0.883 (upper bound 1.11 < 1.43 margin): 5x5Gy + CAPOX noninferior to long-course CRT in LARC.
details: 🔍 Multicenter open-label phase III, 16 Chinese hospitals, N=599 (TNT 302 / CRT 297), median f/u 35.0mo
🔍 cT3-4 and/or cN+ distal or middle-third rectal ca; 85.8% vs 83.5% stage III; MRF+ 56% both arms
📐 RT technique: all pts IMRT. TNT 5Gy x5; CRT 50Gy/25fx with concurrent capecitabine 825mg/m² BID

📐 CTV covered mesorectum, presacral space, internal iliac + obturator nodes, ischiorectal fossa; external iliac only if cT4b; superior border sacral promontory, inferior 2-3cm below tumor; CTV→PTV 0.5-1.0cm
📊 3y MFS 77.1% vs 75.3%, HR 0.88 (0.63-1.24), p=.475: no distant-metastasis gain, unlike RAPIDO/PRODIGE 23
📊 3y OS 86.5% vs 75.1%, HR 0.67 (0.46-0.97), p=.033 (secondary EP, open-label, unadjusted for multiplicity)
⚠️ OS gain is the weak link: no MFS or LRR difference to explain it, and Polish II's early OS benefit vanished at 8y
📊 pCR + sustained cCR 21.8% TNT vs 12.3% CRT, p=.002; cCR 11.1% vs 4.4%, organ preservation without surgery 9.4% vs 3.4%
📊 RT delivery favored short-course: all TNT pts completed 5Gy x5 without dose reduction vs 1.4% dose reduction and 2.4% interruption in CRT
⚠️ Preop grade III-V toxicity 26.5% vs 12.6% (p<.001), driven by hematologic 15.8% vs 2.0%: the cost is chemo, not RT
🔗 3y LRR (8.4%/11.0%) in line with RAPIDO and PRODIGE 23 (4%-8.3%) and far below Polish II (21%-22%), where all pts got IMRT here
⚠️ Preop completion 82.6% vs 95.2% and full-dose 74.8% vs 93.2% (both p<.001): the TNT advantage was postop, 60.0% vs 48.3% completing planned adjuvant cycles (p=.009)
⚠️ Chinese-only population, age 18-70, median 55: younger than a typical Western LARC cohort

details.text: 📊 Grade 3-4 acute toxicity during preoperative treatment
📐 OS subgroup HRs favoring TNT (Fig 3), the only ones reaching significance

details: ⚠️ Those two OS subgroups are unadjusted post-hoc splits of an already-secondary endpoint; DFS was flat in both (cT4 HR 0.621, ≤5cm HR 0.706)
⚠️ Surgical burden similar: grade III+ complications 14.0% vs 15.7% (p=.625); R0 91.5% vs 87.8% (p=.189)

verdict.rationale: Prespecified noninferiority met with adequate power in a randomised phase III; aligns with Polish II, RAPIDO, PRODIGE 23 supporting short-course TNT as a recognized option.
verdict.audience: cT3-4 and/or cN+ distal or middle-third rectal adenocarcinoma, age 18-70

studies.significance: For an RT reader the real finding is delivery, not survival: every TNT pt finished 5Gy x5 with no dose reduction vs 1.4% reduced and 2.4% interrupted on 50Gy/25fx, and 3y LRR stayed at 8.4% with IMRT and standard mesorectal plus internal iliac coverage. The excess grade 3-4 toxicity was hematologic (15.8% v 2.0%), so shortening the RT course costs one week of clinic time, not local control.
studies.monday_clinic: In cT3-4 or node-positive middle or low rectal cancer heading to TME, this supports 5x5Gy followed by CAPOX as an alternative to 50Gy/25fx chemoradiation when treatment-time compression or adjuvant chemo compliance is the constraint; it does not extend to upper-third tumors or pts over 70, neither of whom were enrolled.

primary_endpoint.name: 3-year disease-free survival
primary_endpoint.stat_detail: HR 0.883 (one-sided 95% CI to 1.11), P < .001 for noninferiority

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Multicenter **open-label randomized phase III** noninferiority trial, 1:1, N=599, 16 hospitals across 11 Chinese provinces, accrued Aug 2015 to Aug 2018. Stratified by location, clinical stage and MRF status; median follow-up **35.0 months**. Prespecified NI margin **HR 1.43** (equivalently an 11% absolute DFS margin), one-sided alpha 0.05, ≥194 events for 80% power.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Age **18-70**, ECOG 0-1, **cT3-4 and/or node-positive** rectal adenocarcinoma of the distal or middle third, no distant metastases and no prior anticancer treatment. Median age 55, **MRF involvement 56%** in both arms, clinical stage III in 85.8% vs 83.5%. Staging was **central MRI** read independently by three radiologists; recurrent disease and second primaries excluded.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: TNT arm received **5 Gy x 5** over one week, CRT arm **50 Gy in 25 fractions** over 5 weeks with concurrent capecitabine 825 mg/m² BID. **All patients received IMRT**, the only one of the four TNT trials to do so. CTV covered mesorectum, presacral space, internal iliac, obturator nodes and ischiorectal fossa, external iliac only for cT4b; superior border at the sacral promontory, inferior 2-3 cm below the tumor, CTV to PTV expansion 0.5-1.0 cm with 95% PTV coverage.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: TNT: four cycles of CAPOX (oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² day 1, capecitabine 1,000 mg/m² BID days 1-14) starting 7-14 days after RT, then TME, then **two** postoperative CAPOX cycles. CRT: concurrent capecitabine, TME, then **six** postoperative CAPOX cycles. TME was recommended 6-8 weeks after preoperative treatment in both arms, with watch-and-wait permitted for cCR.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary: 3-year DFS** (locoregional failure, distant metastasis, second primary or death from any cause). Secondary: OS, MFS, locoregional recurrence, surgical complications, toxicity and completion rates, plus rates of radical resection and complete response.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Noninferiority was met and locoregional control was equivalent. The **3y OS difference (86.5% v 75.1%, HR 0.67) is a secondary endpoint** with no corresponding MFS or LRR signal to explain it, and disappeared on subgroup analysis.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: Preoperative grade III-V toxicity **26.5% v 12.6%** (P < .001), almost entirely hematologic (grade 3-4 **15.8% v 2.0%**), with thrombocytopenia 11.1% v 0.7%. GI and proctitis grade 3-4 did not differ. Grade III+ surgical complications 14.0% v 15.7% (P = .625) with no 30-day postoperative deaths; adjuvant-phase grade III-IV toxicity was **lower** with TNT (3.3% v 11.8%, P = .003).

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: 3y LRR of 8.4% and 11.0% match RAPIDO and PRODIGE 23 (**4%-8.3%**) and sit far below Polish II (**21%-22%**). Unlike RAPIDO and PRODIGE 23, STELLAR showed **no reduction in 3-year distant metastasis** (22.8% v 24.7%); like Polish II it showed an early OS gain, which in Polish II had vanished by 8 years.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents cT3-4 or node-positive middle and distal rectal adenocarcinoma in patients aged 18-70 treated with IMRT and oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy. Does not represent upper-third rectal tumors, patients over 70, or the unresectable fixed cT3/cT4 population that dominated Polish II.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: The 11% NI margin was wide, and the authors concede a narrower margin or larger sample would have been preferable in retrospect. Late toxicity and quality of life are deferred to a future report, so the durable pelvic cost of 5 Gy x 5 in this cohort is unmeasured; 53 patients who did not achieve cCR refused surgery, blurring the TME denominator.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Compressing 50Gy/25fx to 5Gy x5 cost nothing in local control (3y LRR 8.4% v 11.0%, p=.461) with IMRT and mesorectal plus internal iliac coverage, and every TNT pt completed RT without dose reduction. The excess grade 3-4 toxicity was hematologic (15.8% v 2.0%), from the CAPOX, not the pelvis. Late toxicity is still unreported.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Moving CAPOX in front of surgery raised completion of planned adjuvant cycles to 60.0% v 48.3% (p=.009) and cut adjuvant grade III-IV toxicity to 3.3% v 11.8% (p=.003), but four preop cycles bought no distant control (3y MFS 77.1% v 75.3%, p=.475). Sequencing, not intensity, is what changed.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: Preoperative sequence did not degrade the operation: R0 91.5% v 87.8% (p=.189), grade III+ complications 14.0% v 15.7% (p=.625), no 30-day deaths, median stay 8 days in both arms. Sustained cCR without surgery reached 9.4% v 3.4%, so more low tumors arrive as watch-and-wait candidates.

papers.title: Total Neoadjuvant Therapy With Long-Course Radiotherapy Versus Chemoradiotherapy in High-Risk Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer (TNTCRT): A Multicenter, Randomized, Phase III Trial
papers.abstract: PURPOSE High-risk locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) carries a substantial risk of distant recurrence, which limits disease-free survival (DFS). We compared total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) integrating long-course radiotherapy (LCRT) with uninterrupted doublet chemotherapy (doublet-LC TNT) versus conventional neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT). METHODS In this multicenter, randomized, phase III trial, patients with stage II/III LARC and at least 1 high-risk feature (cT4a-b, cN2, mesorectal fascia involvement, or cT3c-d with extramural vascular invasion) were enrolled. Patients were assigned to doublet-LC TNT (induction, concurrent, and consolidation capecitabine plus oxaliplatin with LCRT) before surgery or nCRT (capecitabine with LCRT) followed by surgery and adjuvant chemotherapy. The primary end point was DFS (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03177382 ). RESULTS Between June 6, 2017, and December 27, 2023, 458 patients were randomly assigned to doublet-LC TNT (n = 232) or nCRT (n = 226). At a median follow-up of 51 months, doublet-LC TNT improved 3-year DFS (74.8% v 66.0%; hazard ratio [HR], 0.674 [95% CI, 0.489 to 0.929]; P = .016). Metastasis-free survival (MFS; 77.7% v 67.6%; HR, 0.655 [95% CI, 0.469 to 0.915]) and pathologic complete response rates (pCR; 26.37% v 9.80%; P < .001) were higher with doublet-LC TNT, whereas locoregional failure remained low and comparable (6.03% v 6.19%; P = .943). Although grade ≥3 adverse events during the neoadjuvant phase were more frequent with doublet-LC TNT (27.59% v 8.56%; P < .001), severe toxicities during the entire treatment course (28.02% v 24.32%; P = .371) and major postoperative complications (3.98% v 2.94%; P = .567) were comparable. CONCLUSION Compared with conventional nCRT, doublet-LC TNT improved DFS, MFS, and pCR rates with manageable toxicity. These findings support this intensified, doublet-based regimen as a standard option within the modern TNT paradigm. Further comparative studies are warranted to evaluate these results against other short-course radiotherapy‑based or nondoublet-concurrent TNT regimens.

papers.title: Multicenter, Randomized, Phase III Trial of Short-Term Radiotherapy Plus Chemotherapy Versus Long-Term Chemoradiotherapy in Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer (STELLAR)
papers.abstract: PURPOSE To ascertain if preoperative short-term radiotherapy followed by chemotherapy is not inferior to a standard schedule of long-term chemoradiotherapy in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer. MATERIALS AND METHODS Patients with distal or middle-third, clinical primary tumor stage 3-4 and/or regional lymph node–positive rectal cancer were randomly assigned (1:1) to short-term radiotherapy (25 Gy in five fractions over 1 week) followed by four cycles of chemotherapy (total neoadjuvant therapy [TNT]) or chemoradiotherapy (50 Gy in 25 fractions over 5 weeks, concurrently with capecitabine [chemoradiotherapy; CRT]). Total mesorectal excision was undertaken 6-8 weeks after preoperative treatment, with two additional cycles of CAPOX (intravenous oxaliplatin [130 mg/m 2 , once a day] on day 1 and capecitabine [1,000 mg/m 2 , twice a day] from days 1 to 14) in the TNT group and six cycles of CAPOX in the CRT group. The primary end point was 3-year disease-free survival (DFS). RESULTS Between August 2015 and August 2018, a total of 599 patients were randomly assigned to receive TNT (n = 302) or CRT (n = 297). At a median follow-up of 35.0 months, 3-year DFS was 64.5% and 62.3% in TNT and CRT groups, respectively (hazard ratio, 0.883; one-sided 95% CI, not applicable to 1.11; P < .001 for noninferiority). There was no significant difference in metastasis-free survival or locoregional recurrence, but the TNT group had better 3-year overall survival than the CRT group (86.5% v 75.1%; P = .033). Treatment effects on DFS and overall survival were similar regardless of prognostic factors. The prevalence of acute grade III-V toxicities during preoperative treatment was 26.5% in the TNT group versus 12.6% in the CRT group ( P < .001). CONCLUSION Short-term radiotherapy with preoperative chemotherapy followed by surgery was efficacious with acceptable toxicity and could be used as an alternative to CRT for locally advanced rectal cancer.
